summary: LLM health-check agent failing to register in prod AWS account due to STS delegation policy rejecting session
description:
Issue summary:
The LLM health-check agent that runs periodic self-checks and registers service endpoints with the prod cloud-account registration-service is failing to obtain a short-lived STS session. The STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity call returns an AccessDenied error with a context that indicates an attribute-based delegation policy rejected the session because the SAML assertion did not include the org:env attribute.

Impact:
- Health-check agent unsuccessful in registering ~30% of dedicated node pools in us-west-2.
- Alerts on service-registration topic firing intermittently; some canary routing fallbacks triggered.
- Potential risk for automated failover/rolling restarts not being recorded in central inventory.

Environment:
- prod account: aws-prod-123456789012 (us-west-2)
- Component: dedicated-provisioner -> registration-service -> auth proxy -> STS assume-role path
- Agent version: 2026.02.15-rc3

Steps to reproduce:
1. Deploy health-check agent image 2026.02.15-rc3 to a new dedicated pool in us-west-2.
2. Observe registration logs (agent -> registration-service) for AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity call.
3. Check CloudTrail event for sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity and IAM policy evaluation details.

Observed logs / errors:
- Agent logs: "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity failed: AccessDenied: The SAML assertion is missing required attribute 'org:env'"
- CloudTrail: "eventName": "AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity", "errorMessage": "Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity on resource arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/llm-registration-role"
- IAM policy simulator trace points to a DENY in org-wide delegation policy (org-policy-id: ORG-DELEG-2025) that enforces attribute whitelist for SAML/OIDC sessions.

Expected behavior:
- Agent should be able to complete a delegated STS session and register the pool. The registration-service should fall back to alternate short-lived credential flow only if delegation is not permitted by org policy.

Workaround attempted:
- Temp: Manual invocation of AssumeRole with a fully-populated SAML assertion from the ops identity provider allowed registration to proceed.
- Workaround for customers: run the agent with a pre-provisioned long-lived service principal (not acceptable for long-term).

Request / Next steps:
- Triage policy mismatch with Identity team to confirm whether org attribute 'org:env' should be required for these agent-initiated flows.
- If policy is intended, update the agent's OIDC/SAML assertion generation path (auth-proxy) to include org:env attribute for dedicated pools.
- Short-term: create an allowlist exception for the registration-service role for existing dedicated pools while patch is implemented.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC - Initial ticket created after oncall saw 12 failed registrations in last 15m (alerts: registration.failures.high). Reporter: Angela Park.
Checked CloudTrail events for sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity - consistent AccessDenied with missing attribute in assertion. Confirmed by security-tooling trace.

Reviewed org delegation policy ORG-DELEG-2025: policy enforces Condition: StringEquals: saml:attributes/org:env to allowed list [prod, staging]. The agent assertion did not include this attribute (agent auth-proxy uses minimal claim set).

Auth-proxy (auth-proxy v1.4.2) code path: when running as daemon for fleet agents it serializes only 'sub' and 'aud' claims. OIDC bridge library change in 2026.01 removed attribute injection for backward-compatibility - likely regression.
Reproduced locally by forging an OIDC assertion without org:env and calling AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity -> AccessDenied. With org:env present the call succeeds.
Consequence: any agent instance bootstrapped via the current auth-proxy cannot register unless the IdP supplies org:env or auth-proxy is patched.
Linked to PR for auth-proxy fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-proxy/pull/392 (work-in-progress).
comments: Angela Park (2026-03-10 09:18 UTC): Observed spike at 09:05UTC. Affected pools: dp-14, dp-19, dp-21. Opening ticket and looping in Marco.
Marco Ruiz (2026-03-10 10:02 UTC): Acknowledged. I will validate IAM policy and reproduce. Adding identity@redwood for visibility.

Priya Raman (identity team) (2026-03-10 11:30 UTC): We rolled out ORG-DELEG-2025 in Feb to enforce env tagging on SAML/OIDC. That should not break internal agent flows. Can you attach CloudTrail event id?
Marco Ruiz (2026-03-10 12:05 UTC): CloudTrail event id: 7b3f2c1a-... Attached trace in investigation notes. Pinpointed auth-proxy claim omission as likely cause.

SRE Lead - Jordan Miles (2026-03-11 08:20 UTC): As a short-term mitigation, we can add an allowlist for role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/llm-registration-role scoped to instance-profile principal, but prefer an auth-proxy fix.
Angela Park (2026-03-11 09:10 UTC): Customer impact - some internal canaries failed but no customer-facing SLA breaches yet. Proceed with patch and exception plan.

Marco Ruiz (2026-03-12 14:45 UTC): Patch landed to auth-proxy (PR #392). Deploying canary to staging, then will roll to prod registration-service config to include org:env. Leaving ticket open until full roll-out and verification.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 15:30 UTC - Auth-proxy patch merged: inject org:env claim for agent registration flows. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-proxy/pull/392
Temporary allowlist created for role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/llm-registration-role scoped to instance-profile principal on 2026-03-11 10:00 UTC (ops action id OPS-REG-001).
Canary deployment of patched auth-proxy to registration-service succeeded in staging (2026-03-12 12:10 UTC). Production rollout scheduled in maintenance window 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC.
Follow-up: Identity team to audit other internal agent flows for missing attributes (task INT-883999 assigned).
Ticket to be closed after 48h of stable registration metrics in prod (post-rollout verification).
